$comment: Voice registry. Authored stories reference registry KEYS only, never an engine voice name, so a voice can be swapped (for example when American voices are approved) by editing this file and re-running the voice tool; textSha is unchanged but the voice differs, so the lock goes stale and only that voice's clips are re-recorded. Owner of this file after the contract commit: voiceover-tool (speeds and notes); keys are a contract.

engine.name: kokoro
engine.run: local, CPU, seed 0, HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1; reuse the CI-Common venv at ~/.cache/ci-video-kit/kokoro. No cloud TTS, no API key.
engine.fallbacks: Piper is not used (its live engine is GPL-3.0 and per-voice licences vary). macOS say is a last resort only and must be labelled in the lock.

rules: Never voice a child. Children appear in the third person, read by the narrator.
Narrator: one voice per family (casting.json narrator). Third person, present tense.
Agent lines (beat.say): the companion's voice, a different key from the narrator and from the other companions in the same family.
Every voice is synthetic and disclosed (disclosure synthetic-voice). No voice imitates a real person.

pending.$comment: Needs the owner to approve a download of small .pt voice files (about 0.5 MB each) from huggingface.co/hexgrad/Kokoro-82M/voices. Not usable until approved. With them the fleet gains American accents and better-graded voices; the mapping then moves by editing `kokoro` above.

encoding.loudness: per clip -16 LUFS integrated, limiter at -3 dBTP before AAC; post-decode gate: true peak <= -1.0 dBTP and |dI| <= 0.7 LU
encoding.codec: AAC-LC 32 kbps mono 24 kHz in .m4a, -fflags +bitexact, no metadata (plays on every browser including iOS Safari)
encoding.fileName: <beatId>[.say].<hash10>.m4a where hash10 = first 10 hex of sha256(file bytes); stored at content/families/<slug>/audio/
encoding.budget: about 4.4 KB per second of speech; at most 700 KB of audio per family
